A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FIPER and have readable text, equations, tables, and figures. However, v2 refers to supplementary implementation details and multi-frame SR comparisons that are absent from the supplied PDF. Their inclusion in v3 supports comparison of documentation, but limits judgments about whether those methods and experiments were newly introduced.

before.justification: v2 reports original super-resolution, single- and multi-image compression, and image-regression experiments, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and supplies additional video SR results, ablations, timing measurements, and visual comparisons in its appendix.

M1.justification: The shared SR/compression architecture, modulation, losses, and basis-merging pipeline remain substantially intact. Appendix D newly describes temporal VSR processing, whose earlier specification is unavailable. Main equations also change coefficients from c_i to c_ij, while Appendix Equation 17 retains c_i. The PDFs do not resolve whether these differences represent procedural changes or disclosure and notation changes.

E1.justification: v3 substantially expands documented coverage through REDS and Vimeo-90K training and REDS4, Vimeo-90K-T, and Vid4 video evaluation, plus 1D signal-fitting examples. Existing still-image datasets remain. v2 only references multi-frame SR in unavailable supplementary material, so this establishes newly documented coverage rather than when those experiments were first performed.

E2.justification: AsymLLIC and CCA are added to the compression curves in v3 Figure 8, and CCA enters Table 2. The supplied video comparison adds BasicVSR++, VRT, RVRT, PSRT, and IA-RT in Table 6. The main SISR comparator set in Table 1 is retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported SR pretraining learning rate from 1e-4 to 2e-4 and batch size from 16 to 32, retaining 300k pretraining iterations. These are explicit setting revisions; unchanged Table 1 scores do not establish that experiments were rerun. Previously unspecified VSR settings are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained SR-prior and factorization ablations, v3 revises the frequency/convergence analysis and adds 1D/2D examples, smaller-model frequency variants in Table 5, frozen-coefficient and scratch-training merging controls in Table 7, and component/runtime-scaling analyses in Tables 8–9.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing. The new timing averages divide costs among images; they do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 3, 4 and existing Table 2 entries retain their values. Added results include CCA at -20.97% BD-rate beside the retained FIPER result of -21.09%, video SR PSNRs of 32.67/38.09/27.95 in Table 6, and extensive ablation, timing, and visual results. These are additional reported results, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a mathematical development from Fourier representations to spatially varying coefficients and learned nonuniform bases in Equations 1–6. Appendix B additionally formalizes factor-field special cases and the compression model. This is a limited derivational expansion, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden potential applicability from joint SR/compression toward low-level vision generally and emphasize replacing existing networks’ output representations. The central representation claim and headline 204.4% and 9.35% performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving spectral bias, learned coordinates, and modulation-induced high-frequency errors. Appendix E discusses initialization-dependent merging behavior and compensation by coefficients; Appendix F clarifies amortized compression costs. The existing limitations concerning real-time computation and semantic information remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies previously unavailable channel dimensions, Swinv2 block structure, downsampling instructions, coefficient construction, temporal processing and training schedules, and staged basis-compression training details. Detailed architecture diagrams accompany these disclosures. v3 also adds a project-page URL; its online contents were not checked.

R1.justification: The positioning expands from factor-field and architecture comparisons to explicit contrasts with CosAE, local texture/frequency representations, Fourier feature mappings, and spectral-bias research. Video-restoration and newer compression references are added, while the earlier Fourier-space-loss and wavelet-domain-loss citations are removed.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change from Factorized Fields to Factorized Features. The abstract and contributions are reframed, related work is substantially condensed, and Section 3.1 is extensively rewritten into a staged explanation. Supplementary Sections A–H add a substantial document structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds new analytical plots, detailed architecture figures, Tables 5–9, and extensive qualitative comparison sheets. Existing pipeline and SR illustrations are retained or relocated, while compression plots revise legends, axes, and zoom regions. The 1D example is redisplayed in Figures 4 and 9 rather than constituting two separate analyses.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves important documentation gaps in the supplied v2 by providing implementation details and the promised video SR evaluation. Added modulation and merging controls strengthen support for central design choices, while timing breakdowns clarify shared-basis costs. Coefficient notation remains inconsistent, and the unchanged 9.35% headline needs clarification against the newly included CCA comparator, but the gains in reproducibility and evidential support are substantial.
